questiontext.text:
The triangle \(ABC\) below has vertices \(A={@ntupleify(A)@}\), \(B={@ntupleify(B)@}\) and \(C={@ntupleify(C)@}\).

Using only the construction tools provided (which include angle bisector and perpendicular tools), construct the centre of the inscribed circle (the incentre) of triangle \(ABC\), and its inscribed circle.

GeoGebra displays the coordinates of the points you construct. Read off the position of the incentre and the radius of the inscribed circle (the inradius), and enter them below, each rounded to 3 decimal places.

[[geogebra set="A__fixed,B__fixed,C__fixed" width="1200px" height="600px"]] params["material_id"]="dcdnc4ee"; /* Restricted compass-and-straightedge toolbar. customToolBar OVERRIDES the file's toolbar; numbers are GeoGebra tool IDs, | starts a new menu. 0 Move, 6 Delete | 1 Point, 5 Intersect, 501 Point-on-object | 2 Line, 15 Segment, 18 Ray | 10 Circle(centre,point), 53 Compass. */ /* params["appName"]="geometry"; */ params["showToolBar"]=true; params["customToolBar"]="0 | 6 | 5 | 2 | 10 | 9 | 4 | 8 | 38"; params["showToolBarHelp"]=false; /* Hide the algebra input bar and menu bar. NOTE: the algebra VIEW panel is governed by the saved file (perspective is ignored with material_id), so ALSO close the Algebra View in the GeoGebra material and re-save. */ params["showAlgebraInput"]=true; params["algebraInputPosition"]="bottom"; params["showMenuBar"]=false; params["showResetIcon"]=true; params["showFullscreenButton"]=true; [[/geogebra]]
Incentre \(I = (\,\) [[input:xc]] \(,\) [[input:yc]] \(\,)\) \( (\,\)[[validation:xc]], [[validation:yc]] \(\,)\)
[[feedback:prt1]]
Inradius \(r = \) [[input:r]] [[validation:r]]
[[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The centre of the inscribed circle is the incentre: the point where the three interior angle bisectors meet. It is the unique point equidistant from all three sides, so the perpendicular distance from it to each side is the same — that common distance is the inradius \(r\).

Construction. Bisect any two interior angles (say at \(A\) and \(B\)) using the angle-bisector tool; their intersection \(I\) is the incentre. Dropping a perpendicular from \(I\) to any side gives the inradius.

[[geogebra set="A__fixed,B__fixed,C__fixed" width="1200px" height="600px"]] params["material_id"]="pgd3hywq"; /* Restricted compass-and-straightedge toolbar. customToolBar OVERRIDES the file's toolbar; numbers are GeoGebra tool IDs, | starts a new menu. 0 Move, 6 Delete | 1 Point, 5 Intersect, 501 Point-on-object | 2 Line, 15 Segment, 18 Ray | 10 Circle(centre,point), 53 Compass. */ /* params["appName"]="geometry"; */ params["showToolBar"]=true; params["customToolBar"]="0 | 6 | 5 | 2 | 10 | 9 | 4 | 8 | 38"; params["showToolBarHelp"]=false; /* Hide the algebra input bar and menu bar. NOTE: the algebra VIEW panel is governed by the saved file (perspective is ignored with material_id), so ALSO close the Algebra View in the GeoGebra material and re-save. */ params["showAlgebraInput"]=true; params["algebraInputPosition"]="bottom"; params["showMenuBar"]=false; params["showResetIcon"]=true; params["showFullscreenButton"]=true; [[/geogebra]]

For this triangle the incentre is \(I \approx ({@dispdp(ta_X[1],3)@},\ {@dispdp(ta_X[2],3)@})\) and the inradius is \(r \approx {@dispdp(ta_r,3)@}\).

node.description: Both incentre coordinates correct to 3 d.p.?

truefeedback.text: The centre is correctly placed at the incentre.

node.description: Did they find the circumcentre instead?

truefeedback.text: That point is the circumcentre — where the perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet. It is equidistant from the three vertices, not the three sides. For the incircle you must bisect the angles, not the sides.

node.description: Did they find the centroid instead?

truefeedback.text: That point is the centroid — where the three medians meet (the triangle's balance point). The incircle's centre is equidistant from the sides, which you get from the angle bisectors.

falsefeedback.text: Your point \(I\) is not the incentre. The incentre is where the angle bisectors cross — check that each bisector makes equal angles with the two sides meeting at that vertex.

Your inradius is not correct (to 3 decimal places). The inradius is the perpendicular distance from the incentre to any side, equal to \(r = \dfrac{\text{area}}{s}\) where \(s\) is the semi-perimeter.
